entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts by OpenAI bear on this problem; neither claims to settle it. (1) 'Invariant-projection counterexamples for every irrational rotation' (27 Sept 2026): for each irrational θ in (0,1) it constructs a continuous f: circle to [0,1] with f^{-1}(0) = {1} and ∫log f dm = −∞, so the Fuglede–Kadison determinant is 0. The operator T_f = U f(V) in the hyperfinite II₁ factor R_θ has no projection p in R_θ with 0 < τ(p) < 1 and (1−p)T_f p = 0. This answers negatively the Zhu–Fang–Shi question about affiliated invariant subspaces, with the angle fixed in advance. Its quasinilpotence corollary gives T_f nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent. Its transitive-commutant corollary derives, on every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace, whose commutant is a proper strongly closed transitive unital algebra. (2) 'Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant' (27 Sept 2026): by a separate construction on H_0 = L²(Z₂, μ; ℓ²(Z)), it gives a bilateral weighted shift S with fibre weights β_j(x) = exp(−a_j(x)), where the a_j are explicit functions of the 2-adic residues of x; ‖S‖ = e^{−10}; ‖Sⁿ‖ ≤ exp(−10⌊(n+1)²/4⌋); and a commuting contraction V with (Vf)(θx) = V_x f(x). The algebra generated by S, V and all scalar multipliers is transitive, so the commutant of S is transitive. Its abstract presents the result as a negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space.
entries.delivers: Does not settle the problem as frozen, and the manuscripts do not claim to. The frozen problem asks whether every bounded operator on every complex Banach space has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace. The family gives negative answers to two neighbouring questions. (a) Paper 2 answers the hyperinvariant variant: on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space there is a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace. Paper 2 frames the question as whether every nonscalar bounded operator on such a space has one, so its statement of that variant is matched by this construction. A hyperinvariant subspace is in particular invariant, so having none is a weaker property than having no invariant subspace; the operator here does have invariant subspaces. (b) Paper 1 answers, for each irrational θ, the narrower question whether T_f has a nontrivial invariant projection inside R_θ. Its own introduction says invariant subspaces of the Hilbert-space representation need not be affiliated with R_θ, so these are not excluded. Both operators have ordinary invariant subspaces: paper 2 names the tails L²(X; K_{≥h}) as closed, nonzero, proper and S-invariant, and says the invariant and hyperinvariant problems 'must remain distinct'; paper 1's appendix notes the same kind of tail invariance for its product model. Hence neither manuscript gives an operator on a Hilbert space lacking nontrivial invariant subspaces, and neither proves that every operator has one. The matching pass's 'variant' label is accurate: the hyperinvariant result bears on a variant, and the frozen problem is not touched.
entries.remains: Everything in the frozen problem remains open: the question over all complex Banach spaces, including the separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert case, since every operator built here has nontrivial invariant subspaces and so is no counterexample to it. Paper 1's result covers only irrational θ, and its invariant-projection conclusion concerns only the factor R_θ.
entries.direction: disproves the hyperinvariant-subspace variant (paper 2, and paper 1 by a route through its factor result); disproves, for each irrational θ, the variant asking for invariant projections in R_θ (paper 1); does not decide the invariant-subspace problem
entries.object: Paper 2: an explicit bilateral weighted shift S on L²(Z₂, μ; ℓ²(Z)) with weights β_j(x) = exp(−a_j(x)), where the a_j^± are given by formulas in the residues x mod 2^m, and an explicit contraction V built by a recursion normalised by its supremum. Paper 1: a continuous weight f on the circle with f(1) = 0, built in stages (divisible frequencies, ordered couplings, smoothing and relocation of logarithmic drops, a background cost at the zero). Its construction is not a closed formula. The measurable model f_* = exp(−Σ c_i ⌊{q_i x} + {q_i θ}⌋) is explicit but is not the continuous operator the theorem concerns.
entries.conditional_on: Paper 2 uses two lemmas from paper 1, the scalar-multiplier field lemma (its Lemma 3.1) and the commutant lemma (its Lemma 1.2). Paper 1 proves both in its text, and paper 2 says so, so this is a dependency on a manuscript rather than an unproven hypothesis. Paper 1 depends on no other manuscript. Neither result assumes an unproven hypothesis.
entries.doubts: Paper 1 says its hyperinvariant corollary contradicts a hyperinvariant-subspace assertion of Cho, Ko and Lee (Corollary 2.8, p. 801) at μ = 1 (its Remark rem:ckl). That is the manuscript's own claim about a published result, which I have not checked. I found no sketched steps, hedges, or abstract-versus-theorem mismatches in either text; the search for such language matched only routine uses. Paper 1's obstruction argument is asymptotic ('for sufficiently large j'), and its constants are stated but I did not recheck them.
